How to read this result

This is an uncalibrated model score, not a guaranteed chance of churn. Changing an input is a hypothetical scenario, not evidence of cause and effect.

All inputs must fall within the training data's observed ranges. Valid ranges do not guarantee a realistic combination.

Split integrity

Which inputs matter globally?

Validation permutation importance

Bars show the drop in average precision when one input is shuffled, averaged over five repeats. Correlated inputs can share importance. These are not individual explanations or causal effects.

Scope and limitations

Prediction window

UCI documents nine months of input observations and churn status at month 12. The three-month gap is the prediction window; exact customer-level dates are unavailable.

Conservative input selection

Status and customer value are excluded because their operational meaning or derivation needs additional verification. Age and age group are also excluded. This does not establish fairness.

Repeated records

Repeated records are retained because stable customer IDs are absent. Identical model-input profiles are grouped into a single split to reduce duplicate leakage.

Before real business use

This historical dataset comes from one telecom company. External and temporal validation, calibration, fairness assessment, monitoring, and an intervention experiment remain future work.

Source: Iranian Churn (2020), UCI Machine Learning Repository · DOI 10.24432/C5JW3Z · CC BY 4.0. Data cleaned, split, and modeled for this project.
